bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow WRITE 1 Crash State: Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write Pl_AES_PDF::flush Pl_AES_PDF::finish Sanitizer: address (ASAN)
bug_description.normalized: While qpdf rewrites the witness PDF with stream decoding enabled, it parses an encrypted stream whose filter chain builds `Pl_AES_PDF -> Pl_ASCII85Decoder -> Pl_Flate`. A crafted stream causes `Pl_Flate` to throw `stream inflate: inflate: data: incorrect header check` during `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::flush`. Because `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::flush` resets `pos` only after its downstream write, the exception leaves `pos == 5` with the completed 5-character group still buffered. The same exception also unwinds through `Pl_AES_PDF::flush` before `offset` is cleared, and `QPDF::pipeStreamData` then calls `finish()` on the same pipeline. `Pl_AES_PDF::finish` therefore re-enters `flush(true)` on stale AES state and forwards another byte sequence into the stale ASCII85 decoder. The first accepted cleanup byte(s) write past `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::inbuf[4]` but remain inside the heap object, corrupting decoder bytes after the 5-byte subbuffer; later accepted iterations of the same `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write` loop continue from that stale/corrupted state until line 85 finally writes beyond the 64-byte allocation and ASAN reports the 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow.

source.description: QPDF starts parsing the attacker-controlled PDF input and materializes the stream dictionaries, raw stream offsets/lengths, and encryption parameters later used by the crashing stream-decoding path.
source.value_from: Attacker-controlled PDF bytes in `poc`, including a `/Encrypt` dictionary with `/StmF/StdCF` and `/CFM/AESV2`, and stream dictionaries whose `/Filter` array is `[ /ASCII85Decode /FlateDecode ]`.

sink.description: The cleanup-triggered second `Pl_AES_PDF::flush` re-enters `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write` while `pos` is still 5. The first accepted cleanup byte(s) begin writing past the decoder's 5-byte `inbuf`, and later accepted iterations of that same loop continue from the stale/corrupted decoder state until the same line-85 store lands outside the 64-byte `Pl_ASCII85Decoder` allocation and triggers ASAN.

root_cause.description: Root cause. `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::flush` forwards the decoded group before resetting `pos` and `inbuf`. If the downstream write throws, the decoder keeps `pos == 5` and stale buffered state; `Pl_AES_PDF::flush` similarly keeps `offset == buf_size`, so cleanup replays another byte sequence into that stale decoder. The first replayed base85 bytes only overflow past `inbuf[4]` inside the object, and later loop iterations then reach the heap redzone. The fix stores the byte count in a temporary, resets decoder state first, and only then calls `getNext()->write(...)`; the same patch also moves `Pl_AES_PDF`'s `offset` reset before its downstream write so cleanup cannot replay the block into the stale decoder.

parser_admitted.description: After parsing/recovery, the writer reaches the witness stream and invokes `object.pipeStreamData(...)` with stream decoding enabled, exercising the encrypted ASCII85/inflate pipeline that crashes.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement reads attacker-controlled raw bytes from the current stream's file range into `buf`; those bytes are then decrypted and fed to the downstream ASCII85 and Flate decoders.

coarse_trace.summary: Parses the attacker-controlled PDF and builds object, stream, and encryption state for later writing.
Reads the parsed `/Filter` metadata, builds a `Pl_ASCII85Decoder -> Pl_Flate` decode chain for the witness stream, and allocates the `Pl_ASCII85Decoder` heap object that is later corrupted.
Because the witness stream is encrypted, qpdf prepends `Pl_AES_PDF` ahead of the ASCII85/inflate chain and then starts piping raw stream bytes through the resulting pipeline.
A decoded ASCII85 group is forwarded to the downstream inflater before the decoder resets `pos`; `Pl_Flate` rejects the decoded bytes and throws, leaving the ASCII85 decoder state stale.

The failed write is cleaned up by calling `finish()` on the same top pipeline. Because `Pl_AES_PDF` also had not reset its block state before the exception, cleanup re-enters `Pl_AES_PDF::flush`, first spills accepted base85 bytes past `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::inbuf[4]` inside the decoder object, and then later line-85 iterations continue far enough to hit the heap redzone.

fine_trace.note: Parses the attacker-controlled PDF into qpdf's internal object model. For the crashing witness, this produces the current stream's `/Filter` metadata, raw file offset/length, and encryption parameters that drive the later decode pipeline.
Reads the witness stream's attacker-controlled `/Filter` entry and copies its names into `filters`. On the crashing path, the parsed filter list includes `/ASCII85Decode` and `/FlateDecode`.

Reverse pipeline construction wraps the sink pipeline with `Pl_Flate` for `/FlateDecode` and then with `Pl_ASCII85Decoder` for `/ASCII85Decode`, so each full 5-character ASCII85 group is turned into 4 binary bytes and sent into the inflater. ASAN later attributes the corrupted heap object to this `new Pl_ASCII85Decoder` allocation.

fine_trace.code: pipeline = new Pl_AES_PDF("AES stream decryption", pipeline, false, QUtil::unsigned_char_pointer(key), key.length());
fine_trace.note: Because the parsed stream is encrypted and resolves to AES decryption, qpdf prepends `Pl_AES_PDF` ahead of the ASCII85/inflate chain. The staged crash stack confirms that this AES arm executed.
Reads attacker-controlled raw bytes from the current stream's file range into `buf` so they can be delivered to the `Pl_AES_PDF -> Pl_ASCII85Decoder -> Pl_Flate` pipeline.

fine_trace.code: std::memcpy(this->inbuf + this->offset, p, bytes); this->offset += bytes;
fine_trace.note: AES decryption buffers the stream bytes into its 16-byte block buffer and advances `offset`. Once `offset` reaches `buf_size`, the current block is ready for `flush(false)`.
With a full 16-byte block buffered, `Pl_AES_PDF::flush` decrypts that block into `outbuf` and forwards it downstream while `offset` is still equal to `buf_size`.
The decrypted block is consumed as ASCII85 text. Each valid character is appended to the decoder's 5-byte group buffer, and when `pos` reaches 5 the decoder enters `flush()` for that completed group.

Root cause. `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::flush` decodes the completed 5-character group buffered in `inbuf` into `outbuf` and forwards 4 bytes while `pos` is still 5. For the witness stream, the downstream inflater rejects that group and throws before lines 124-125 reset the decoder, so `pos` stays 5 and the old group buffer remains live.

The decoded bytes from step 8 are not a valid zlib stream for the downstream `Pl_Flate` stage, so inflate raises `std::runtime_error`. The staged trace witnesses this exact failure mode as `stream inflate: inflate: data: incorrect header check`.

That runtime_error propagates back through the still-active AES downstream write before line 264 executes. The same `Pl_AES_PDF` object therefore keeps the current ciphertext block buffered in `inbuf`, leaves `offset == buf_size`, and has already advanced `cbc_block` for that block.
After the decode error, `success` is still false, so qpdf runs cleanup by calling `finish()` on the same top pipeline instance instead of discarding it.
Because step 10 left `offset == buf_size`, the decrypt-side cleanup path re-enters `flush(true)` on the same `Pl_AES_PDF` object instead of discarding the stale buffered state.

Cleanup-triggered `Pl_AES_PDF::flush` recomputes `outbuf` from the still-buffered AES state and forwards `bytes` bytes to the next pipeline. Here `bytes` starts at `buf_size` (16) and can only be reduced by lines 243-260 because this call uses `strip_padding = true`, so cleanup replays at most one decrypted AES block into the stale ASCII85 decoder.

The cleanup write from step 13 re-enters `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write` while `pos` is still 5 from step 8. The first accepted cleanup byte(s) that reach the default base85 arm therefore write to `inbuf[5]`, `inbuf[6]`, and later positions beyond the 5-byte subbuffer, beginning an out-of-bounds overwrite inside the heap-allocated decoder object.

Because `write()` keeps iterating over the same cleanup buffer, later accepted bytes keep executing line 85 after step 14 has already crossed the `char inbuf[5]; size_t pos; size_t eod;` boundary. Given step 13 replays at most 16 bytes total while ASAN reports the final fault 10 bytes past a 64-byte `Pl_ASCII85Decoder` object, simple counting up from `pos == 5` cannot by itself reach the reported address. The continued in-object overwrites therefore have to advance into the adjacent decoder bookkeeping region before the final reported store.

depends_on.via: bytes after `inbuf[4]` inside the decoder object are already being overwritten

fine_trace.note: Sink. A later accepted iteration of that same cleanup-time line-85 store uses the stale/corrupted decoder state from step 15 and writes beyond the 64-byte `Pl_ASCII85Decoder` allocation. The saved ASAN report witnesses this store at `Pl_ASCII85Decoder.cc:85` and places the faulting address 10 bytes past the allocated object.

depends_on.via: stale/corrupted decoder state after the in-object overwrites

QPDF::pipeStreamData(int, int, long long, unsigned long, QPDFObjectHandle, Pipeline*, bool, bool)

format.name: PDF
format.contract: A PDF that qpdf parses far enough to rewrite streams, containing an encrypted stream whose parsed metadata causes qpdf to build the decode pipeline `Pl_AES_PDF -> Pl_ASCII85Decoder -> Pl_Flate`. The witness stream's bytes must decrypt to ASCII85 data that reaches a full 5-character group and then makes the downstream inflate stage throw `incorrect header check` during `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::flush`, leaving `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::pos == 5` and `Pl_AES_PDF::offset == 16` on the same pipeline instance so cleanup `finish()` re-enters `Pl_AES_PDF::flush(true)` and feeds enough accepted base85 bytes into the stale decoder to first write past `inbuf[4]` and later, during the same `Pl_ASCII85Decoder::write` loop, reach the heap redzone.
